paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computing Simulated Annealing Algorithm Applying in Portfolio Optimization Problem

experiments.description: Quantum annealing/QUBO portfolio optimization model for selecting stocks under a budget constraint, evaluated in Python simulation for risk-seeking and risk-averse parameter settings and compared against DOW index and random buying.

algorithm.variant: quantum annealing applied to QUBO portfolio optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: terminate when transverse field strength Γ reaches 0 or after MaxSteps iterations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initialized state x with corresponding state energy H_pot(x); parameters initialized at start of annealing

optimizer_settings.field_update_rule: Γ = Γ0 / MaxSteps (as written in Eq. 5; exact schedule notation in paper is unclear)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary variable x_i indicates whether stock i is purchased (1) or not (0); portfolio composition expressed in share quantities / binary purchase decisions
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize V = V_return - L * V_risk with budget penalty; return V_return = Σ_i w_i x_i, risk V_risk = Σ_{i,j} cov(i,j) x_i x_j, and constraint penalty H = Σ_i (P_ij x_i - K)^2; final objective given as Q = V - λH + p_i - r (paper notation is partially unclear)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty term added to enforce investment budget constraint

problem_instance.description: Portfolio selection over stocks using historical price/return trends; two investor preference settings (risk-seeking and risk-averse) are simulated

dataset_specification.description: Uses real stock price trends / market data; compares portfolio return time series with DOW index fund and random buying. No ticker list, date range, or preprocessing details reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Not reported beyond computing returns and covariance from stock prices
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Python simulation; results compared visually in time-series plots against DOW index and stochastic buying baseline

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper states that quantum annealing may be superior to simulated annealing when data size is sufficiently large, but does not provide quantitative evidence or a measured speedup.
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime, complexity, or benchmark numbers are reported; superiority is discussed qualitatively only.
